text:
anya: Quick follow-up to the console-query RFC — thinking about pushing RBAC enforcement down into the query service itself instead of fetching full user perms in the console. Goal is to reduce tile latency and limit round-trips. any concerns?
max: sounds promising. main worry is cache invalidation + complexity around org/role changes. if we push checks down we need a strong TTL and cache bump path.
jordan: +1. another option: keep decision in console but send a signed assertion to query service (short-lived) so query can trust it without a full lookup. that keeps audit trail on the console side.
sophia: we should be careful with compliance — logs/audit have to show who authorized what. if query service takes decisions, we need consistent audit events shipped to central logging. also row-level filtering is tricky if logic is duplicated.
anya: good points. use-cases: public dashboards (low-trust) vs internal. perf target: dashboard tile median <200ms. many tiles are heavy aggregations, so extra hop hurts.
max: what about a hybrid: basic coarse RBAC (org/project-level) enforced in query service with a PDP cache, and fine-grained checks (row-level ACLs) in console or a rewrite layer. that limits false negatives and keeps some complexity central.
jordan: implementation thought: add an auth header like `X-Redwood-Assertion: <signed-json>` containing user_id, org_id, allowed_scopes, exp. query service validates signature and caches parsed policy decisions for TTL=30s. fallback: query service can call PDP for misses.
sophia: signed assertions are okay if we keep a rotation plan for keys and rotate frequently. still need end-to-end audit: assertion id + user id must be logged by query service. also, for compliance we might need the original policy hash attached to the log.
max: tradeoffs: signed assertion reduces latency and load but increases risk if assertions are leaked. Mitigation: very short TTL, bind to request fingerprint or route, and encrypt in transit (TLS + mTLS). also monitor assertion reuse patterns.
anya: what about caching behavior for dashboards with many tiles? we should avoid per-tile PDP calls. maybe a batching layer: console requests a single multi-tile statement token that query service can expand.
jordan: prototype API sketch:
```
POST /query/execute
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <service-token>
         X-Redwood-Assertion: {user,org,exp,roles, signature}
Body: {tiles: [{sql, params, tile_id}, ...], require_audit: true}
```
Query service returns per-tile results + audit-id.
sophia: add a `sensitive_columns` hint so query service can automatically redact if policy forbids. also introduce `audit_required` flag that forces console to persist original user context.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: eng-platform/query-service v3.4.0 -> prod-canary (5%) :rocket:
max: rollout plan suggestion: feature flag `queryRbacV2`, enable for internal orgs first, collect metrics: tile_latency, pdp_calls_per_request, assertion_misses, audit_event_rate. rollback if tile_latency increases >10% p50.
anya: owners: jordan -> RFC PR + prototype, max -> perf harness + metrics, sophia -> compliance/audit spec. I'll create follow-up PR and link the RFC. timeline: prototype + tests in 2 weeks, canary in 4.
jordan: I'll pick up PR and add the assertion verifier library. also will mock PDP for tests.
sophia: I'll draft audit schema and key rotation plan. will also add retention and export requirements.
anya: SG. created ticket ENGPLAT-1126 and pinned to board. TL;DR: hybrid enforcement, signed short-lived assertions, PDP fallback, audit hooks required. next: RFC PR and perf tests. :thumbsup:
max: sounds good. I'll add load tests to the dashboard suite and a small sim for assertion replay.
jordan: putting initial branch up today, will drop link in thread when ready.
sophia: noted. will sync with security on key rotation policy.
anya: thanks everyone — feel free to @mention if you want to be looped into the PR review.
